The proliferation of Large Language Models and automated code analysis systems has created a structural gap in existing licensing frameworks. MIT, Apache, and GPL licenses were written before such systems existed. RCF-PL addresses this gap directly.

Additional supporting material:

This license is now accompanied by a peer-reviewed preprint 
formally analyzing its theoretical foundations:

"Restricted Correlation as a Neuromodulation Paradigm: 
Applying Brain Network Control Theory to AI Intellectual 
Property Protection"

DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21085740
Zenodo: https://zenodo.org/records/21085740

The paper establishes structural equivalence between Stanford 
Neuromodulation Therapy (SNT, npj Mental Health Research 2024) 
and RCF-PL, grounding the license in network neuroscience 
literature and providing formal theoretical basis for the 
anti-correlation principle underlying RCF-PL's design.

**On the term "correlation" in this license:**

"Correlation" here refers to a specific technical operation, not a
figure of speech: the process by which an AI model, during training or
inference, extracts a Protected Work's methodology (algorithmic
structure, architectural decisions) and reproduces it — including after
translation into a different programming language, where copying
detection based on text or AST similarity would no longer apply.

Unlike copying, distribution, or modification — which concern the
Protected Work's literal form — restriction of correlation concerns
whether an AI system's internal representation was shaped by exposure
to the Protected Work's methodology. This is why the license introduces
it as a separate restricted act alongside the traditional ones, rather
than folding it into "modification" or "derivative work."
